Local-first work memory for macOS

Find any moment of your work. Pick up where you left off.

FNDR turns the work you allow it to see into checked text memories that stay on your Mac. Search them, ask questions that come back with citations, and reopen the exact source.

Remember
Screen text, OCR and imports become evidence-backed memories.
Find
Search and cited answers share one retrieval path.
Resume
Reopen sources, tasks and saved work sets.

Three separate checks
Different boundaries, not one blanket privacy switch.
1Capture admission
Paused, private and blocked contexts are skipped before any memory is written.
2Read-time visibility
Search, graph, related memories and MCP reads re-check that every source is still visible.
3Review before effects
Each action step runs, asks the person or never runs, judged on real arguments and targets. A model's plan is only a proposal.

Context stays local by default. Thirty-six subsystems follow, three per page, each drawn from source-backed nodes and directed connections.
FNDR is a local-first macOS app that remembers permitted work context as structured text memories with source evidence, and helps a person find and resume it across apps.
Team: Anurup Kumar, Kunj Rathod, Minh Le, Felipe Marin. CS 4500 / Fall 2026. With thanks to Professor Ganesh Gopalakrishnan, the CS 4500 course staff and the open-source maintainers behind FNDR.
Evidence and limits. Declarations were indexed across 728 source files and 248,664 lines, then 106 file and symbol references were checked by targeted inspection; this is not a line-by-line audit. Diagrams record structure, not measured performance or study results. Snapshot: commit 5c92a8a on Nov 16 2026, including uncommitted working-tree content.

Qualifications that hold across every page
  • Capture admission, read-time source visibility and network/action approval are separate boundaries.
  • MiniLM 384-d (memories_v4_minilm_384) is the active parent embedding contract; BGE-large child chunks are an optional separate 1024-d space.
  • Shared retrieval plans, routes, reauthorizes, fuses and decides a strong match; Ask then verifies support before a cited, partial or refused answer.
  • GraphRoute code exists but the active planner does not select it; graph browsing and projection are implemented.
  • Every bulk or derived read re-checks current source visibility; reading the database is not authorization.
  • Exact source statements show what appeared on screen, not speaker, intent, completion, truth or permission.
  • Task suggestions need checked screen evidence; the task/activity daily brief is composed in code from checked fields, not by the on-device 2B model.
  • Heavy local model work is serialized and kept off the async executor; swapping a handle does not prove weights were unloaded.
  • The native microphone actor coexists with renderer recording paths during migration.
  • Screen Guide keeps images and questions ephemeral by default; diagnostics and Memory Journey have separate consent and expiry.
  • Notch Do treats a model plan as a proposal; Rust classifies every effect from arguments and observed target state.
  • Peer delegation reviews an exact payload and destination; peer output is untrusted and grants no local authority.
  • Mobile clients reuse the Mac runtime; the Watch reaches the Mac through the phone; TLS pinning has a missing-pin fallback.
  • A compiled file is not a mounted panel; the separate wiki composer is a stub.
